items.prompt: An EDITOR re-saves their own DRAFT entry with a new summary and the slug it already has. What does updateDraftEntry do?
items.answer: It saves, as the slug lookup leaves out the entry being edited
distractors: 409 "That slug is already in use", as the entry matches itself too
It saves, but the slug gets a numeric suffix to stay unique
400, since an unchanged slug has to be left out of the payload
items.explanation: updateDraftEntry calls findEntryBySlug(input.slug, entryId), and the repository adds NOT: { id: excludeId }, so the entry's own row never counts as a conflict.

items.prompt: Login returns the same "Invalid email or password" for unknown emails and wrong passwords. Can an attacker still tell which emails exist?
items.answer: Yes, by timing: unknown emails skip the bcrypt compare
distractors: No: identical messages make the two cases indistinguishable
Yes, through the HTTP status code, which differs between the cases
Only if the attacker can also read the Session table
items.explanation: Equal messages hide existence in the body but not in latency; the review also notes there is no rate limiting.

items.prompt: Session.token stores the cookie token as-is. What does someone with read access to the Session table gain, and what closes it?
items.answer: Live impersonation of every unexpired session; hashing tokens at rest closes it
distractors: Nothing, because the cookie is httpOnly and cannot be set by hand
Only the user's email; each token is bound to its original IP address
Encrypting the cookie in the browser closes it without any schema change
items.explanation: With a plaintext token, a database read becomes live sessions: paste the token into a cookie. Storing sha256(token) and hashing the cookie at lookup would change only findSessionByToken (lookup) and createSession (write).

items.prompt: Where are expired sessions removed, and which ones are never removed?
items.answer: Deleted when presented after expiry; never-presented ones stay forever
distractors: A nightly job deletes all expired rows using the expiresAt index
Expired rows for every user are deleted whenever anyone logs in
They are never deleted; getSessionFromToken only returns null for them
items.explanation: Eager delete-on-access stops a stale cookie causing repeated reads; Session_expiresAt_idx would support a sweep, but none exists.

items.prompt: Which status transition is reserved for ADMIN only?
items.answer: Restoring an archived entry back to an editable draft
distractors: Publishing an editor's own draft
Archiving a live published entry
Discarding a never-published draft into the archive
items.explanation: canTransitionEntry special-cases ARCHIVED -> DRAFT to require ADMIN; editors self-publish their own drafts with no review step.

items.prompt: An editor requests a PUBLISHED -> PUBLISHED status change on their own entry. Does isValidStatusTransition accept it?
items.answer: Yes: any same-status move returns true before the transition map is consulted
distractors: No: PUBLISHED may only move to ARCHIVED, so the service returns 409
No: the service returns 403 because editors cannot touch published entries
Yes, but only for admins: editors get a 403 from canTransitionEntry
items.explanation: The guide lists this under 'where it falls short': same-status moves pass the check - so a no-op transition can still run the transaction and write an audit row.

items.prompt: The search query string carries featuredOnly=false. What does z.coerce.boolean() produce?
items.answer: true, since Boolean("false") is true
distractors: false, because zod parses the string "false" as a boolean
A validation error
undefined, then the default
items.explanation: z.coerce.boolean() uses Boolean(value), and any non-empty string - including "false" - is truthy. That is why the guide flags it as a weakness of the validation boundary.

items.prompt: A new entry has title "!!! ???" and no slug. What does the save schema do?
items.answer: The derived slug is empty, so the length refine rejects it
distractors: It saves the entry with a random fallback slug of 8 characters
It saves the entry with the literal slug "!!!-???"
The title min-length check rejects it before any slug is derived
items.explanation: The schema normalizes at the boundary: .transform derives the slug from the title when none is given, then .refine guards its length.

items.prompt: How much can an admin's curation add to an entry's search score on top of its text rank?
items.answer: At most 5.25 points
distractors: At most 1.5 points
Unlimited, because manualBoost multiplies the text rank
Exactly 3.75 points
items.explanation: The SQL adds CASE WHEN isFeatured THEN 1.5 ELSE 0 END + manualBoost * 0.15 (0 to 3.75) to ts_rank_cd's text rank, so curation adds at most 5.25.

items.prompt: An editor saves an entry with the tags [" Runbooks ", "Runbooks"]. How many tags does upsertTagsByNames link to the entry?
items.answer: One tag named Runbooks, as names are trimmed before the dedupe
distractors: Two tags, because the dedupe step runs before the names are trimmed
One tag named " Runbooks ", with its surrounding spaces kept
None: the save fails on the unique constraint of the tag slug
items.explanation: upsertTagsByNames maps each name through trim() and then dedupe() (a Set), so both become one "Runbooks" with slug runbooks; one upsert runs and findMany returns that tag. The save schema trims tags as well.

items.prompt: createAuditLog is declared as (client: DbLike = db, input). What is odd about that default?
items.answer: Callers must always pass a client positionally, so the default is never used
distractors: Default parameters are not allowed before required ones in TypeScript
It makes every audit write escape the caller's surrounding transaction
It opens a brand-new database connection for every audit row written
items.explanation: Passing the service's transaction as client is what makes the audit row commit with the change; the default is dead weight.

items.prompt: Which audit action stores the entire request input as its metadata?
items.answer: knowledgeEntry.curated
distractors: knowledgeEntry.updated
knowledgeEntry.statusChanged
knowledgeEntry.created
items.explanation: createAuditLog(..., metadata: input) in curateEntry; update events by contrast record only the slug, not a diff - and nothing reads the audit log yet.

items.front: updateDraftEntry (knowledgeEntryService.ts:121-130) checks ownership and canEditEntry but not status. What is the consequence?
items.back: Editors can silently rewrite already-PUBLISHED content through the editor form, with no review step - combined with self-publishing, nothing stands between an editor and live knowledge-base text.

items.front: GET /api/tags (route.ts:4-11) calls listAvailableTags with no session check. What leaks?
items.back: Tag names created on unpublished drafts are visible to anonymous users - a side channel into work in progress. Require a session (and filter to tags on published entries for viewers).

items.front: This app's isolation is author ownership, not tenancy. List what adding a tenantId would have to touch.
items.back: KnowledgeEntry, Tag (slugs and names are globally unique today), AuditLog, Session/User, all three find* scopes, the raw search SQL WHERE plus its tag sub-select, and GET /api/tags.

items.prompt: The search page has loaded. A user types vpn into the search box one letter at a time. How many search requests follow, and what does the result list show while each is in flight?
items.answer: Three, and each new key shows the loading state first
distractors: One, after typing pauses, as the hook debounces input
Three, with the previous results kept on screen
One, as all filters share one key that refetches
items.explanation: The query text is React state passed straight into useKnowledgeSearch (search-dashboard.tsx:20-26), and the hook puts the whole filters object in the key, ["knowledge-search", filters] (useKnowledgeSearch.ts:30-33). Every keystroke is a new key, so v, vp and vpn each start a fresh query; nothing debounces. A new key has no data, and without placeholderData the result is isLoading true with data undefined, which the page renders as its loading state (search-dashboard.tsx:131). A probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.99.0 (the lockfile version) showed requests for v, vp and vpn, each with isLoading true and no data, and no request when the key went back to vp within the 30 s staleTime.

items.prompt: An editor views the search page, goes to the workspace, creates a draft with the brand-new tag Payments, and returns to search via the header link 10 s later. Do the tag filter chips include Payments?
items.answer: No, as the cached tag list is fresh and never invalidated
distractors: Yes, as the create mutation also invalidates the tag list
Yes, as the search page refetches its tags on each mount
No, as the server page passes in the tags at render time
items.explanation: Every entry mutation invalidates ["workspace-entries"], ["knowledge-search"] and, for edits, the entry's own key (useEntryMutations.ts:23-28 and the three hooks after it), never ["tags"]. The tag chips come from useTags with key ["tags"] (useTags.ts:13-18), and the client's staleTime is 30 s (app-providers.tsx:8-17). Returning within 10 s mounts the query onto cached, still-fresh data, so React Query does not refetch it; a probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.99.0 fetched the tags once, left them un-invalidated through the entry invalidations, and did not refetch on remount. The search page receives only the session from its server component (src/app/page.tsx), and the chips come from this client query, so Payments shows up once that query refetches.

items.prompt: A developer sorts the workspace list in the browser with b.updatedAt.getTime() - a.updatedAt.getTime(), since WorkspaceEntry types updatedAt as Date. What happens?
items.answer: tsc passes, and the sort throws a TypeError at runtime
distractors: tsc fails, as the client type marks updatedAt a string
It sorts correctly, as apiClient revives the ISO dates
tsc passes, and the sort silently compares as NaN
items.explanation: mapWorkspaceEntry puts real Date objects into publishedAt and updatedAt (knowledgeEntryRepository.ts:421-422), and the shared WorkspaceEntry type says Date (types/knowledge.ts:31-32), so the server side is consistent. apiOk serializes with NextResponse.json (responses.ts:6-8), and JSON has no date type, so the browser receives ISO strings; apiClient returns payload.data cast to T without reviving anything (client.ts:19). The compiler trusts the type, so the code compiles, but a string has no getTime method and the call throws a TypeError (a JSON round-trip probe on Node 22 gave typeof string, getTime undefined). The existing components avoid this only because they wrap the value in new Date(...).

items.prompt: An editor submits the workspace form with a 10-character summary; the schema requires at least 20. What message does the form show?
items.answer: The request payload is invalid, with no field named
distractors: The summary needs at least 20 characters, under that field
Request failed, as the 400 body has no message
Unable to save entry, as the error is not an Error
items.explanation: The form has no client-side length rules, so the request is sent. The route's parse throws a ZodError, and apiError turns it into a 400 whose body is { error: { code: INVALID_REQUEST, message: "The request payload is invalid", issues } } (responses.ts:23-34; the summary rule is knowledgeEntrySchemas.ts:41). apiClient reads only payload.error.message and throws a plain Error with it (client.ts:13-17), so the flattened issues that name the summary field never leave the fetch wrapper, and the workspace shows that message (workspace-dashboard.tsx:124-126). The status and the code are dropped too, so no caller can branch on them.

items.prompt: An entry was first published on 1 March and archived on 1 April. An admin restores it to draft and publishes it again on 1 May. What does its publishedAt hold now?
items.answer: 1 May, as every move to PUBLISHED overwrites the date
distractors: 1 March, as the first publish time is never changed
null, as archiving clears it and nothing sets it again
1 April, as it records the most recent status change
items.explanation: updateKnowledgeEntryStatus writes publishedAt: status === PUBLISHED ? new Date() : null on every status change (knowledgeEntryRepository.ts:348-353). Archiving on 1 April therefore set it to null, the restore to DRAFT (allowed only for an ADMIN, permissions.ts:71-73) kept it null, and the publish on 1 May set it to that moment; changeEntryStatus passes every accepted transition straight to this function (knowledgeEntryService.ts:163-179). The column means last published, not first published, and only the createdAt of the March knowledgeEntry.statusChanged audit row still records when it first went live. Search ties are broken by publishedAt, so a republished entry sorts as new.

items.prompt: Two editors create drafts titled VPN Runbook at the same moment, and both slug look-ups run before either insert. What do the two POSTs return?
items.answer: One 201, and one 500 from the unique index on slug
distractors: One 201, and one 409 from the slug pre-check in the service
Two 201s, with the second entry's slug suffixed
One 201, and one 409 mapped from Prisma's P2002
items.explanation: The slug check is a read on the shared client before the transaction opens (knowledgeEntryService.ts:88-92), so when both reads run first, both see no row and both proceed to create (:94-103). The unique index on KnowledgeEntry.slug (schema.prisma:61) lets one insert win and rejects the other with Prisma's P2002, a PrismaClientKnownRequestError. apiError maps only AppError and ZodError, so that error is logged and returned as 500 (responses.ts:36-46). A probe with Prisma 6.19.3 on PostgreSQL 18 reproduced the interleaving: both pre-checks empty, one create fulfilled, the other rejected with P2002. The pre-check is only a friendly message; the index is the guard, and mapping P2002 to 409 would make both paths agree.

items.prompt: A signed-in user opens /entries/vpn-runbook, a published entry. The session lookup succeeds, then the database connection drops before the entry query runs. What does the server page render?
items.answer: The not-found page, as every lookup error becomes null
distractors: The error page, as the failed query throws during render
The entry from the last render, as server pages cache
A redirect to /login, as the page re-checks the session
items.explanation: The page awaits getPublishedEntryBySlug(slug).catch(() => null) and calls notFound() when the result is null (page.tsx:26-30). getPublishedEntryBySlug throws NotFoundError for a missing entry (knowledgeEntryService.ts:49-57), but the catch swallows every rejection, so a connection failure takes the same path and Next.js renders the not-found UI with a 404 status. Without the catch the error would reach the error boundary; the page reads cookies, so it renders per request and has no earlier copy to serve; and the session check ran once, before the lookup. Had the session query itself failed, getServerSession would have thrown, since it catches nothing. Catching only NotFoundError would keep outages visible as errors instead of a misleading not-found.

items.prompt: On the search page a user selects both the runbooks and the security tag chips. Which published entries can the search return?
items.answer: Entries carrying either tag, since any one match counts
distractors: Only entries carrying both tags, as each chip narrows it
Only entries whose tags are exactly runbooks and security
Only entries tagged runbooks, as the first chip is used
items.explanation: Each chip click adds or removes a tag slug in selectedTags (search-dashboard.tsx:79-83), and all of them are sent as repeated tags parameters. The repository turns the list into one EXISTS subquery whose condition is tag_filter.slug IN (...) (knowledgeEntryRepository.ts:160-172), which is true when the entry has at least one of the slugs. A probe on PostgreSQL 18 with that shape returned the runbooks-only, the security-only and the both-tags entry. The chips therefore widen the result, which is the opposite of the narrowing most faceted UIs give; AND semantics would need a GROUP BY with HAVING count(DISTINCT slug) equal to the number of chips, or one EXISTS per tag.

items.prompt: Twelve published entries match a search. A client calls the search API with pageSize 10 and page 3. What does the response's totalCount say?
items.answer: 0, as the count rides on rows and page 3 returns none
distractors: 12, as the window count runs before the LIMIT and OFFSET
2, as the count covers what is left after the offset
400, as page 3 is past the last page for this search
items.explanation: totalCount is COUNT(*) OVER() computed per returned row (knowledgeEntryRepository.ts:249-253). The window count is evaluated before LIMIT and OFFSET, so on pages 1 and 2 every row carries 12. On page 3 the OFFSET of 20 skips all twelve rows, no row comes back, and the mapper falls back to rows.length > 0 ? ... : 0 (:256-263). A probe on PostgreSQL 18 with the same shape gave 12, 12 and then no rows. The schema bounds page only from below, so page 3 is not rejected. A separate COUNT query, as the workspace list uses, keeps the total correct on any page.

items.front: How is the search SQL built, and what keeps user input from becoming SQL?
items.back: One $queryRaw with Prisma.sql: a CTE joins entries to author and tags, groups per entry, aggregates tag names, and, when there is a query, ranks with ts_rank_cd over weighted tsvectors (title A, summary and tags B, content C) against websearch_to_tsquery, keeping matches with HAVING. The query text, tag slugs, page size and offset are bound as parameters by the Prisma.sql template; only fixed fragments are spliced in.

items.front: Which query keys does an entry update invalidate, and why does one call cover every status filter?
items.back: ["workspace-entries"], ["knowledge-entry", entryId] and ["knowledge-search"]. The workspace list is cached as ["workspace-entries", statuses], so each status selection is its own entry; invalidating the ["workspace-entries"] prefix marks all of them stale, and only the mounted ones refetch at once. The same holds for every cached search under ["knowledge-search", filters].

items.front: How do the server pages load data, compared with the client components?
items.back: The pages are async server components: they read the session with getServerSession, and the entry page calls the service function directly, in process, with no HTTP hop and no React Query. The search and workspace dashboards are client components that call /api routes through React Query hooks. So one rule set, the service layer, has two kinds of caller: server pages and route handlers.

items.front: How does saving an entry update its tag links?
items.back: Inside the update transaction the service first resolves the tag rows for the submitted names, then updateKnowledgeEntry rewrites the join rows with tags: { deleteMany: {}, create: [...] }: every KnowledgeEntryTag row for the entry is deleted and the current set re-inserted on each save, changed or not. Tag rows themselves are never deleted, so an unused tag stays in the tags list.
